- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.5) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak values by 5–10%.
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.5), model often underestimates; adjust downward bias by adding 3–7% to forecast to compensate.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +10%+ above recent high); cap forecast at 1.5x recent high for 3–5 days post-spike.
- If sentiment swings sharply (e.g., +1.5 to -1.5 in 3–5 days), model misreads momentum; apply mean reversion: forecast = 0.8×previous day + 0.2×true value if sentiment reverses.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overweights recent volatility; smooth 30d forecast by averaging last 7–10 days’ prices unless sentiment strongly signals trend continuation.
- If sentiment history shows repeated negative spikes (e.g., -1.0+ for 3+ days), model underreacts; add 2–5% to forecast to account for “sentiment lag” correction.
